script.base: PIT leads narrowly in a low-scoring game, with Warren carrying the ground game and offering a short receiving outlet against TB's blitz. TB stays competitive enough to maintain its rushing attack while Otton remains involved underneath; pace data is missing.
script.flip1: TB leads and PIT shifts toward passing. Warren's combined-yardage case can survive through receiving work, but his rushing opportunity becomes less secure; Otton's receiving over becomes more dependent on TB continuing to throw.
script.flip2: PIT builds a substantial early lead and slows the game with rushing. Warren benefits from carries, while TB's comeback passing can support Otton; neither outcome guarantees efficiency or target allocation.

data_check.notes: The written hypotheses are dual-path opportunity for Warren and modest receiving opportunity for Otton; recent totals test those hypotheses rather than independently creating them. Warren produced 163.3 combined yards per game across the supplied three-game window, including 6.55 rushing YPC, but those figures are not a forward projection. Otton produced 39.3 receiving yards on 5.3 targets per game over that window. No projection or simulation was run. Normalizing the supplied paired prices gives a 50.0% market baseline for Warren's combined over and approximately 49.9% for Otton's receiving over; these are not identified Pinnacle prices or estimated true hit probabilities. Warren remains a flagged lean rather than a validated bet; Otton has no direct numerical contradiction in the supplied pack.
data_check.disagrees: TB's 3.61 rushing YPC allowed challenges continuation of Warren's recent 6.55 YPC and therefore the rushing component of his combined-yardage read. PIT's QB EPA/dropback of -0.38 against blitz also challenges the assumption that TB's 41% blitz rate creates productive receiving outlets rather than failed possessions.
data_check.missing: Projection, simulation median, calibrated hit probabilities, Pinnacle prices, full price timestamps, game-level distributions, snaps, routes, positional coverage, actual pressure rates, injuries and weather.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and Warren lost because TB's 3.61-YPC run defense contained his carries while its blitz produced negative plays instead of check-down yardage; the recent 490-yard sample overstated sustainable efficiency. Otton lost because a 38-point-total game offered limited productive passing and Egbuka's 22-target role or Godwin's 14-target role captured the available opportunities. Missing route participation, injury information and positional coverage prevent ruling out either counter-case. Warren's counter-case is substantial enough to flag the read; neither lean merits strong confidence.
slip_story: Both candidates fit a narrow PIT lead: Warren contributes on the ground and through short throws while Otton receives opportunities as TB stays competitive or chases. A TB-controlled rushing game weakens Otton, so this pairing is not script-proof. Do not force a 3–4-leg slip from two candidates or add unsupported legs. No wager placed. The pack lacks an exact pre-kickoff logging timestamp, persistent read/hash record and postgame results; no lock or postmortem is claimed.
